Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the SOBHA Limited Q2 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by ICICI Securities Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines will 
be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after 
the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please 
signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note that 
this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Adhidev 
Chattopadhyay from ICICI Securities Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Adhidev Chattopadhyay: Hello. Good evening, everyone, and I’d like to welcome everyone on the SOBHA Limited call 
today. From the management, as always, we have with us Mr. Jagadish Nangineni, the 
Managing Director; and Mr. Yogesh Bansal, the Chief Financial Officer. I’d now like to hand 
over the call to the management for their opening remarks and comments. Over to you. 
Thank you. 
Jagadish Nangineni: 
Thank you, Adhidev. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining today’s call for Q2 
and H1 2027 earnings. I extend a warm welcome to all our investors, analysts and 
stakeholders. I’ll briefly highlight our business performance and key developments before I 
hand over to our CFO, Yogesh Bansal. H1 ’27 was the strongest half year in the SOBHA’s 
history with sales value of INR5,862 crores, a strong 47.2% year-on-year growth. 
We sold 3.76 million square feet across 2,260 units, with sales volume growing at 32.4%. 
SOBHA’s share of sales value also reached a record of INR4,874 crores. In Q2 FY27, this is 
our second highest quarterly sales of INR2,206 crores with a growth of 16% year-on-year 
with 1.42 million square feet across 828 units. 
Average price realization improved to INR15,522 per square feet in Q2 from INR13,648, 
representing 13.7% growth. For H1, realization increased to INR15,604 per square feet 
compared to INR14,028 last year, reflecting our strong product positioning and favorable 
sales mix. From a city wise market performance point of view, Bangalore remained our 
largest market, contributing INR3,385 crores or about 58% of first half of sales, and NCR 
of about INR1,974 crores which is, again, about 34%; Kerala at INR357 crores, which is 
about 6% and remaining cities at 2.5%. 
Following significant launches in Q1 and Q2, Q2 witnessed healthy sustenance sales, 
particularly from our launched project in Q1, SOBHA OneWorld and SOBHA Neopolis in 
Bangalore and SOBHA Crescent and Aranya in Gurgaon. This demonstrates sustained 
customer demand beyond the initial launch phase. Overall, we are on track for our guidance 
and hopefully exceed in terms of sales for the entire financial year. 
Coming to new launches. During this quarter, we launched 2 projects, this is SOBHA 
Boulevard, which is a plotted development project in Mysore and SOBHA Bellevue, high-rise 
and apartment project about 4.3 acres, 298 homes of about 0.8 million square feet in 
Calicut. Overall, for the first half, we launched 5 projects across Bangalore, Gurgaon and 
Calicut, aggregating to 7.91 million square feet with an estimated sales potential of close to 
INR11,200 crores. 
On forthcoming launch pipeline remains robust at 20.42 million square feet across 18 
projects. We are quite confident of launching at least 9 projects, exceeding 11 million square 
feet during the remainder of FY27. As of September 30, 2026, our unsold inventory stood 
at approximately 15 million square feet, providing a healthy growth visibility.

On execution front, we completed 720 homes covering 1.49 million square feet across 9 
wings and blocks in Q2. H1 completion stood at 1,391 homes covering 2.56 million square 
feet across 17 wings. Coming to cash flows and financial briefly, Our balance sheet continues 
to be our key strength. We maintained a net cash position of about INR322 crores with a 
competitive borrowing cost of 7.75%. And remaining focused on sustaining 0 net debt 
position throughout FY27. We achieved our highest ever cash inflows for both for the 
quarter and half year. Q2 collections reached more than INR2,000 crores at INR2,084 and 
our net operational cash flow was INR422 crores. This financial strength supports our future 
investments while maintaining prudent capital allocation.  
As of end of this quarter, we had INR 22,040 crores of revenue yet to be recognized from 
units already sold. We expect -- while the quarter level margins appear lower, we continue 
-- as we continue to recognize lower margin projects and as we recognize future projects, 
which we are on course for completion and handovers, we are quite confident that our 
margins will significantly improve, and we should be able to deliver at least over 50% growth 
of PAT over last financial year, by the end of this financial year. 
During Q2, our contracts, manufacturing and retail businesses generated about INR225 
crores, an increase of 31% quarter-on-quarter and the external order book stood at INR540 
crores. Our commercial rental portfolio contributed INR24 crores in income during the 
quarter. We expect these businesses to maintain steady performance and with scope for 
marginal growth. 
Also in this quarter, as part of our plan to deepen our expertise in terms of execution, we 
have acquired a small business of fire and safety from SOBHA Projects and Trade Limited 
(SPTL) and this would enable us to execute fire protection services across all our projects 
as we scale towards a larger volume delivery. 
With this remarks, I will conclude my opening remarks, and then I will hand over the forum 
to our CFO, Mr. Yogesh Bansal for his remarks on the financial performance. 
Yogesh Bansal: 
Good evening, everyone. Let me take you through the key financial highlights of SOBHA’s 
performance for the second quarter and first half of FY27. The first half has been marked 
by strong operational continued investment in project execution and expansion of our 
development pipeline while maintaining a healthy balance sheet. 
We recorded our highest ever half yearly operation cash inflow, INR4009 crores, generated 
positive operational cash flow of INR755 crores and closed September with a net cash 
position of INR322 crores. Coming to cash flow, operational cash inflow for the quarter 
stood at INR 2084 crores compared with INR 2046 crores in the corresponding quarter last 
year. 
The real estate collection contributed INR1,922 crores. Again, this operational outflow was 
INR1,642 crores, resulting in positive operational cash flow of INR442 crores  quarter-on-
quarter. For the first half, operation cash inflow reached INR4,009 crores with positive 
operational cash flow of INR755 crores. 
Construction expenditures continue to be an important area of cash deployment. During the 
quarter, real estate project-related outflow stood at INR826 crores while sales and 
marketing expenditure was INR103 crores. We have made land payment amounted to 
INR617 crores during quarter 2 and INR987 crores for the first half.

These payments are aligned with our objective of strengthening the development pipeline 
while continuing to fund existing projects. After accounting for land payments, capital 
expenditure and financing-related movement, the overall net cash movement was negative 
INR337 crores for Q2 and negative INR486 [crore] for H1. Our operation continues to 
generate positive cash flow while we deployed capital towards existing projects and further 
growth. 
Moving to our reported financial performance, total income for quarter stood at INR1,017 
crores compared with INR1,469 crores in Q2 of the previous year. Real estate revenue 
contributed INR749 crores while contractual, manufacturing and retail operations 
contributed to INR225 crores. Quarterly EBITDA stood at INR119 crores reprojecting a 
margin of 11% while profit after tax was INR33 crores. 
For the first half, total income stood at INR2,347 crores, EBITDA was INR249 crores in profit 
after tax amounted to INR84 crores Our gross debt as on 30th September 2026 stood at 
INR1,505 crores against cash and cash equivalent of INR1,827 crores. Our debt-to-equity 
ratio stood at negative 0.07 while average borrowing cost was 7.75%. 
Maintaining financial discipline remains a key priority. We continue to focus on optimizing 
borrowing costs, maintaining adequate liquidity and balancing investment in new 
opportunity with the funding requirement of ongoing projects. Looking ahead, our existing 
portfolio provides meaningful visibility on future cash flow and revenue. 
As of 30th September 2026, receivable from sold unit together with sale value of unsold 
inventory stood at INR31,814 crores against estimated remaining project cost of INR19,297 
crores. This represents projected project level marginal cash flow of INR12,517 crores. 
Including forthcoming projects, the projected state project level margin cash flow increased 
to INR19,748 crores. This figure provides visibility on the potential of our existing 
development portfolio. 
To conclude, our priority remains clear, sustaining operating cash generation, progressing 
project execution, maintaining balance sheet strength and ensuring disciplined capital 
allocation. We remain committed to delivering sustainable growth, strengthening financial 
performance and creating long-term value for our shareholders. 
Thank you. We can now take your questions.
